title: introduce-pricewatch-prefetch-heuristics-and-quant-profile-admin-api
author: Evan Morrison
description: Motivation: Tenant workloads vary widely; static batching/cache defaults and a single quant profile lead to avoidable unit-costs for small/medium tenants. This PR adds a lightweight decision agent (PriceWatch) that recommends tenant-scoped prefetch/batching heuristics and a catalog of compact quantization profiles exposed through a restricted admin API. The goal is safe automatic suggestions (not forced changes) that reduce token-cost and GPU time while preserving latency SLOs. What this PR does: 1) runtime: introduce PriceWatch agent module that samples request streams and computes a small set of candidate prefetch strategies (none, prefix-KV prefetch on hot routes, microbatch windows) and maps them to quant profiles (fp16, int8-llm, int8-q4_0) with confidence scores; 2) admin API: adds POST /v1/admin/pricewatch/evaluate and GET /v1/admin/pricewatch/profiles for operators to preview suggestions and bulk-apply or export profiles; 3) telemetry: new metrics pricewatch.suggestions.count, pricewatch.applied.count, pricewatch.delta_cost_estimate, and per-tenant sampling histograms; 4) rollout safety: feature-flag gated, dry-run default, per-tenant rollback hooks and automatic fallbacks to existing tenant defaults when latency regressions are detected; 5) tests & benchmarks: unit tests for decision heuristics, integration test in the prefilling integration harness, and a smoke benchmark showing ~6-11% token-cost reduction on two sampled customer workloads with tail-latency within SLA in canary. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-4872) - [x] runtime agent implementation - [x] admin API + RBAC gating - [x] telemetry + dashboards - [x] unit/integration tests - [x] canary run & perf summary - [x] docs snippet in /docs/admin/pricewatch.md Safety notes: quant profiles are only recommended; any applied change requires operator approval or an explicit tenant opt-in for auto-apply. Rollout plan: enable dry-run for all tenants by default for 1 week, monitor pricewatch.delta_cost_estimate and tail latency; enable auto-apply for low-risk tenants after 2 weeks if delta_cost_estimate stays negative and no regressions. Related: builds on earlier prefilling/quant work (ENG-3921, PR refs) and aligns with SUP-1187 support case to reduce runaway costs for a mid-market tenant.

review_comments: Anika: Please add a short circuit for routes tagged 'no-prefetch' so we never sample restricted flows. (done)
Marco: Can you include a quick safety threshold: if p95 latency increases by >5% revert auto-applies for that tenant? (added and tested)
Tess: RBAC gating looks good but ensure GET endpoint does not leak tenant-specific samples; use aggregated buckets. (fixed: aggregation added)
QA: Integration bench shows cost reduction but saw flakiness on tiny workloads, recommend longer warmup in canary (addressed)
release_notes: Add PriceWatch agent and admin API to suggest tenant-scoped prefetch and quant profiles; dry-run by default; opt-in auto-apply and telemetry. Operators can preview and apply suggestions via the admin API.
performance_summary: Canary microbenchmarks against two sampled tenant workloads: workload A (conversational): 8.7% estimated token-cost reduction, 0.9% median latency change, p95 within SLA; workload B (batch ranking): 6.1% estimated token-cost reduction, median latency unchanged. Bench harness details in integration-tests/prefill/README.
test_plan: Unit tests cover heuristics and edge cases. Integration test runs full sampling loop in the prefilling harness. Canary run executed on a subset of tenants with dry-run enabled, then two low-risk tenants with operator-approved auto-apply. Monitoring: pricewatch.delta_cost_estimate, tail latency per route, error rates. Rollback triggers based on p95 latency or error spike.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: suggestions only until operators opt into auto-apply. Future follow-ups: a UI in Console to review suggestions, a tenant-scoped scheduler to apply low-risk changes automatically after a probation period, and offline model to better predict quantization quality tradeoffs.
merge_summary: Merged after approvals from Anika and Marco and a successful canary run. Squashed commits into a single changelog entry and updated docs. No rollback required post-merge.
